_nota: Inglés del Paso 1 · La evaluación inicial. Calco parcial. Las siglas de estrategia (ETC, EAC, DCO, SDS, MuST) ya son inglesas y se dejan tal cual; Tscherne y Gustilo-Anderson conservan su nombre. «Índice de shock» es shock index, y «déficit de base» base deficit.
subtitulo: The patient first, not the radiograph
preguntaClave: Is this patient — and this skin — in a fit state to be operated on, and when?
sintesis: The patient first. The physiological category (stable, borderline, unstable, in extremis) determines the surgical strategy (ETC, EAC, DCO, MuST); the soft tissues (Tscherne/Gustilo, with mechanism and contamination as reclassifiers) determine what can be done and through where. Above all of it, compartment syndrome: if there are suggestive or established signs, decompressive fasciotomy comes before any other part of the plan. The remaining steps are executed on that foundation.
objetivos: Classify the polytrauma patient as stable, borderline, unstable or in extremis using objective physiological variables
Choose the surgical strategy that matches each category (ETC · EAC · DCO · SDS · MuST)
Grade the soft tissues with Tscherne (closed) and Gustilo-Anderson (open), including the IIIA/IIIB/IIIC breakdown
Recognise that macroscopic contamination or contact with organic material define type III on their own
Recognise compartment syndrome before the late signs appear

decisiones.pregunta: Which physiological category is the patient in?
decisiones.ayuda: The patient's physiology — not the clock — dictates the surgical strategy. The values are assessed dynamically and together, never as isolated single readings.

criterios: No vasopressors · 0–2 units of packed red cells
Low-dose vasopressors · 3–10 units of packed red cells
Medium to high-dose vasopressors · > 10 units of packed red cells
≥ 5 of the 7 in extremis criteria → mortality > 50%
SBP < 90 with no response · vasopressor dependence · massive transfusion protocol
Lactate > 4 with no clearance · pH < 7.20 · base deficit < −14

decisiones.ayuda: It follows from the physiological category. The engine suggests it and warns you if you choose another.

criterios: Definitive fixation of every fracture within 24 h
Borderline patient who responds to resuscitation
Definitive fixation at 24–36 h if the parameters normalise
Phase 1 within 24 h: external fixator + ICU
Life-saving surgery only: haemorrhage control, fasciotomies, minimal provisional fixation
No intramedullary nailing and no definitive surgery

decisiones.pregunta: What is the state of the soft tissues?
decisiones.ayuda: An open fracture is graded AFTER debridement, not in the emergency department: the skin wound underestimates the deep injury.

criterios: Minimal injury or superficial abrasion from pressure from within
Arterial disruption or established compartment syndrome (III)
Extensive damage BUT adequate bone cover by soft tissue
Segmental fractures, gunshot wounds, high energy — type III whatever the size of the wound
Arterial injury REQUIRING repair to save the limb

decisiones.pregunta: Are there signs of compartment syndrome?
decisiones.ayuda: It is ALWAYS asked, alongside the soft-tissue grade and independently of it: an open fracture does not decompress the compartments. Suspicion is clinical; pressure is measured only when the clinical picture cannot be assessed.

criterios: Pain proportionate to the injury and controlled with the usual analgesia
Pain out of proportion or increasing despite analgesia
Pain on passive stretch of the toes or fingers
Compartment tight and tense on palpation
Patient not assessable (obtunded, intubated, regional block): measure pressures — ΔP = diastolic BP − compartment pressure < 30 mmHg is an indication
Wooden-hard compartment with an established neurological deficit
Paraesthesia, paresis or pallor present (LATE signs)
Do not wait for further studies: the diagnosis is already made

decisiones.ayuda: Contamination reclassifies: certain mechanisms are type III by definition, whatever the size of the wound.

criterios: Type III by definition, whatever the size of the entry wound
Cavitation and deep devitalisation from dissipation of kinetic energy
Clothing and contaminants dragged into the track
Explore the whole track, not just the holes
Soil, sand, grit or visible foreign bodies
Farmyard, barn, manure or faecal matter

reglas.texto: Definitive fixation of every fracture within 24 h.
Definitive fixation at 24–36 h if the parameters normalise. If they plateau or worsen, escalate to DCO.
Phase 1 within 24 h: external fixator and ICU. Definitive conversion between day 5 and day 10.
Life-saving surgery only. Definitive conversion deferred to day 5–10 or later, if the patient survives and normalises.
Decompressive fasciotomy comes before all of the above; definitive fixation is subordinate to it.
Arterial repair rules: rapid stabilisation to protect it, and vigilance for compartment syndrome after reperfusion.
Early flap cover (fix and flap); the definitive procedure is planned together with the plastic surgery team.
Serial debridement before any definitive step; do not close primarily.
Also conditioned by the soft-tissue window: wait for the wrinkle sign and for the blisters to settle.

esencial.texto: The fracture never exists in a vacuum. The method begins with the patient: what physiological state they are in, how the soft tissues are, and when it is best to operate. It is the ground on which most technically well-fixed fractures end in failure.
If the skin or the patient is not ready, the best implant is the wrong one. The patient's physiology — not the clock — dictates the surgical strategy.

esencial.titulo: Physiological variables · B. Metabolic / blood gases
Physiological variables · D–F. Temperature, oxygenation and neurological

esencial.texto: PaCO₂ > 50 · Hb < 9.5 · pH < 7.2 · lactate > 4 · base excess < −6 · shock index > 1 · P/F < 300. With ≥ 5 of 7 positive, mortality exceeds 50%.

esencial.titulo: Resuscitation endpoints — clearance for definitive surgery
filas: Lactate ≤ 4 (ideally < 2) · base deficit ≥ −5.5 · INR < 1.5 · temperature > 35 °C · SBP > 90 without vasopressors · lactate clearance > 10 %/h · platelets > 100,000 · Hb > 8. Reassess within 24–36 h. There is no fixed time window: physiological normalisation is the only valid criterion.

If the parameters improve steadily, definitive fixation with close monitoring. If they plateau or worsen, escalate to DCO. Independent aggravating factors: severe head injury (GCS ≤ 8), bilateral pulmonary contusion (P/F < 200), bilateral femoral fracture, ISS > 40, vasopressors, age > 65, frailty.

Life-saving surgery only: haemorrhage control, fasciotomies if there is compartment syndrome, minimal provisional fixation. No intramedullary nailing and no definitive surgery. Conversion deferred to day 5–10 if the patient survives and normalises.

esencial.titulo: Lactate clearance — the dynamics of the response
Surgical strategies — for whom and when
filas: Early definitive fixation if the physiology allows it
Minimal surgery (external fixator) + ICU + deferred conversion
Definitive surgery only when it is safe; it integrates the team's resources and experience
Life-saving surgery only; no definitive fixation
Phase 1 immediate and minimal · definitive day 5–10+

esencial.texto: Trauma releases DAMPs and activates complement: SIRS proportional to the magnitude of the injury, plus the lethal triad (coagulopathy + hypothermia + acidosis). Operating definitively on a physiologically compromised patient amplifies the SIRS towards ARDS and multi-organ failure. Reamed intramedullary nailing generates the largest second hit (EPOFF, Pape 2003).

Coagulopathy (INR > 1.5 · platelets < 100,000 · fibrinogen < 150) + hypothermia (temperature < 33 °C, which worsens the coagulopathy and causes dysrhythmias) + acidosis (pH < 7.25 · base deficit < −10 · lactate > 4, which inhibits the clotting enzymes). Active prevention: warming blankets, warmed fluids, a warm theatre.

filas: Low energy; minimal or no injury. Simple fracture line.
Abrasion or superficial contusion from pressure of a fragment from within.
Significant muscle contusion; deep contaminated abrasion; moderate to high energy.
Extensive crushing, closed degloving, arterial disruption or compartment syndrome.
Clean, from inside out; minimal contusion; low energy
Antibiotics + debridement; fixation according to the fracture
Moderate damage; no extensive avulsion or flaps
Extensive damage BUT adequate bone cover; segmental, gunshot
No flap required; fixation according to physiology
Periosteal stripping and bone exposure; massive contamination
REQUIRES a flap; early fix and flap
Arterial injury requiring repair to save the limb

esencial.titulo: Mechanism and contamination reclassify: type III by definition
esencial.texto: Regardless of the size of the wound, these are type III: gunshot wounds, macroscopic contamination (soil, sand, foreign bodies), contact with organic material (farmyard, barn, manure, faecal matter), standing water, segmental fractures and those presenting late. A 5 mm entry wound is not a Gustilo I if a bullet caused it: the kinetic energy is dissipated along the track and the real damage is deep. Farmyard settings and manure add the risk of clostridia: serial debridement and broadened antibiotic cover.

esencial.titulo: Mechanisms that define type III regardless of wound size
filas: The kinetic energy is dissipated along the track: cavitation, deep devitalisation and contaminants dragged in. The skin wound does not reflect the damage.
High energy and devascularisation of the intermediate fragment.
Massive organic contamination; risk of clostridia.
Atypical flora (Aeromonas, Vibrio); broadened antibiotic cover.
It demands serial debridement; the bed is not left clean in a single sitting.
Extensive devitalisation even when the skin looks intact.

items: Early antibiotics: time to antibiotics weighs more than time to theatre.
Debridement and lavage: the viability of the bed defines the result; serial if there is macroscopic or organic contamination.
Stabilise and cover (fix and flap): early flap in IIIB.
Tetanus prophylaxis according to immunisation status and degree of contamination.
Local antibiotics (beads, sponges, impregnated cement) as a complement to systemic ones.

esencial.titulo: Compartment syndrome — the diagnosis is clinical and there is only one course of action
esencial.texto: Suggestive or established signs demand immediate decompressive fasciotomy. There is no intermediate course: not observation, not elevating the limb, not waiting for an MRI. Remove every circumferential dressing and the cast down to skin while theatre is being prepared. In the patient who cannot be assessed, ΔP (diastolic pressure minus compartment pressure) < 30 mmHg confirms the indication; in the assessable patient, the clinical picture is enough and measuring pressures must not delay surgery.

esencial.titulo: Compartment syndrome — the sequence of signs
filas: Pain out of proportion and increasing despite analgesia
Pain on passive stretch of the digits
The most reliable in the conscious patient
It supports suspicion; a soft compartment does not exclude it
A warning sign that is frequently ignored
The last to appear: the limb is usually lost

items: Decompress EVERY compartment of the segment: in the leg, four through a two-incision approach (anterolateral and posteromedial).
Long incisions: a short fasciotomy is an incomplete fasciotomy.
Assess muscle viability with the 4 Cs — colour, consistency, contractility and capacity to bleed.
Do not close primarily: delayed progressive closure or a graft once the swelling settles.
Definitive fixation is subordinate to the decompression: temporary stabilisation if needed.
Watch for rhabdomyolysis and renal function after reperfusion.

esencial.texto: In the pilon, calcaneus, tibial plateau and ankle, definitive surgery is deferred until the swelling settles. The return of the skin creases (wrinkle sign) and the resolution of the blisters signal that the skin will tolerate the incision. In the meantime: spanning external fixator or traction.

alertas.texto: Suspicion is clinical and it can arise at any point in the course: pain out of proportion and pain on passive stretch are the early, reliable signs. Paraesthesia, pallor, paralysis and absent pulse are late. In the patient who cannot be assessed, measure pressures. Reassess serially.

With ≥ 5 of 7 criteria positive, life-saving surgery only: haemorrhage control, fasciotomies if there is compartment syndrome and minimal provisional fixation. No intramedullary nailing. Definitive conversion is deferred to day 5–10 if the patient survives and normalises.

alertas.titulo: Borderline: the decision is taken on the trend, not on a single reading
alertas.texto: If the parameters improve steadily, definitive fixation with close monitoring. If they plateau or worsen, escalate to DCO. A lactate clearance below 10 %/h obliges you to defer.

alertas.titulo: Reamed nailing is the largest second hit
alertas.texto: In the unstable or in extremis patient, reamed intramedullary nailing amplifies the inflammatory response towards ARDS and multi-organ failure (EPOFF, Pape 2003). External fixator and deferred conversion.

There are signs of compartment syndrome. Decompression comes before any other part of the plan: remove dressings and circumferential cast down to skin, theatre without delay, decompress every compartment of the segment through long incisions. Definitive fixation is subordinate to the fasciotomy; temporary stabilisation if needed.

alertas.titulo: Open does not exclude compartment syndrome
alertas.texto: An open fracture does NOT necessarily decompress the compartments and does NOT rule out a compartment syndrome. Keep watching.

Arterial repair takes priority over definitive fixation. Rapid stabilisation (external fixator) to protect the repair, a joint vascular team, and close vigilance for compartment syndrome after reperfusion.

alertas.titulo: Gunshot wound — type III by definition
alertas.texto: Do not classify by the size of the hole. Explore the whole track, not just the entry and exit wounds; look for dragged clothing and fragments. Debride the track, give early antibiotics and watch closely for compartment syndrome. A track running close to a vascular axis obliges you to exclude arterial injury.
Farmyard settings, manure and faecal matter demand serial debridement, broadened antibiotic cover and a low threshold for returning to theatre. Do not close primarily.
Its value loses reliability in the intoxicated, diabetic, chronically renally impaired or elderly patient. In those cases, rely on the base deficit and on the trend, not on an isolated value.

alertas.titulo: A fragility fracture is a sentinel event
alertas.texto: It announces the next one. It demands specific anchoring strategies (fixed angle, augmentation) and secondary prevention.

alertas.titulo: Talar dislocation: the reduction does not wait
alertas.texto: A Hawkins III or IV keeps the talar body extruded, tenting the skin from within with its blood supply interrupted. Urgent reduction is the only thing that can save that skin and some of the blood supply, even if definitive fixation is deferred.

alertas.titulo: This is the pelvic pattern that bleeds
alertas.texto: Open-book and vertical shear increase the pelvic volume and tear the presacral venous plexus. Pelvic binder or external fixator from the outset, massive transfusion protocol, and an early decision about packing or angioembolisation. Definitive fixation comes afterwards.

reglasCoherencia.titulo: Consistency — definitive strategy in an unstable patient
reglasCoherencia.mensaje: You chose a definitive fixation strategy in an unstable patient. The physiology does not authorise it: damage control (DCO) and deferred conversion on day 5–10.
The strategy chosen is not the one that matches the selected physiological category. Check whether there is an aggravating factor that justifies it.
In extremis with a definitive strategy: mortality > 50%. MuST only — life-saving surgery.
Compartment syndrome: decompressive fasciotomy comes before the whole plan. No later step is carried out before decompressing.

reglasCoherencia.titulo: Caveat — fasciotomy is authorised within MuST
reglasCoherencia.mensaje: Fasciotomy is one of the few operations authorised in the in extremis patient: it is part of life-saving surgery (MuST).

evidencia.afirmacion: The classification into four physiological categories (stable, borderline, unstable, in extremis) and its thresholds come from a PRISMA systematic review of 1,550 publications.
Reamed intramedullary nailing in the at-risk polytrauma patient amplifies the immunoinflammatory parameters compared with damage control (EPOFF).
EAC protocol: lactate ≤ 4 mmol/L or base deficit ≥ −5.5 after resuscitation authorises early definitive fixation (n = 1,239).
In extremis score of 7 criteria: with ≥ 5 positive, mortality exceeds 50%.
Early intravenous antibiotics reduce infection in open fractures; the classic «6 hours» limit for debridement is not well supported.
Salvage versus amputation (LEAP): similar functional results at 2 and 7 years; the MESS does not reliably predict the need to amputate.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: Why is an open fracture graded after debridement and not in the emergency department?
opciones: Because there is not enough time in the emergency department
Because the skin wound underestimates the deep injury
Because the grade only matters for the operation note
Because the classification requires prior radiographs
autoevaluacion.explicacion: The true grade — above all IIIB/IIIC — is only known once the debrided bed is seen. The skin lies about what lies beneath.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: High-energy closed tibial fracture with blisters and tense swelling. Operate definitively today?
opciones: Yes, the sooner the better for healing
Yes, if the patient is haemodynamically stable
No: stabilise temporarily and wait for the soft-tissue window
No: treat definitively without surgery
autoevaluacion.explicacion: Step 1 overrules the radiograph. Fixator or cast, and wait for the wrinkle sign.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: What is the earliest and most reliable sign of compartment syndrome?
opciones: Absent distal pulse
Pallor and coolness of the limb
Pain out of proportion and pain on passive stretch
Paralysis of the compartment musculature
autoevaluacion.explicacion: The classic Ps (pallor, paraesthesia, paralysis, pulselessness) are LATE signs. Waiting for them is arriving too late.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: A patient with a lactate of 3.2 mmol/L falling by 15%/hour after resuscitation. Category and conduct?
opciones: Stable — ETC, definitive fixation of everything within 24 h
Borderline responder — individualised EAC with close monitoring
Unstable — DCO mandatory
In extremis — life-saving surgery only
autoevaluacion.explicacion: A lactate of 2–4 with a clearance of 10–20 %/h defines the borderline responder. The decision is taken on the trend, not on the single reading.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: How many of the 7 in extremis criteria are needed to predict a mortality above 50%?
opciones: 3 of 7
4 of 7
5 of 7
7 of 7
autoevaluacion.explicacion: The 7 criteria are PaCO₂ > 50, Hb < 9.5, pH < 7.2, lactate > 4, base excess < −6, shock index > 1 and P/F < 300. With ≥ 5 positive, mortality exceeds 50%.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: Unstable polytrauma patient with a femoral shaft fracture. Which step is expressly contraindicated?
opciones: External fixation of the femur
Reamed intramedullary nailing
Temporary skeletal traction
Fasciotomy if there is compartment syndrome
autoevaluacion.explicacion: Reamed nailing generates the largest second hit (EPOFF, Pape 2003): it amplifies the SIRS towards ARDS and multi-organ failure. External fixator and conversion on day 5–10.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: A 2 cm wound from a tractor accident, with manure in the bed. Which Gustilo type is it?
opciones: Type I, because the wound is under 10 cm
Type II, from the size and the moderate damage
Type III, because a farmyard setting and organic contamination reclassify by definition
Not classifiable until it heals
autoevaluacion.explicacion: The size of the wound does not rule when there is macroscopic contamination or organic material. A farmyard setting is type III by definition, with an added risk of clostridia: serial debridement and broadened cover.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: What distinguishes a Gustilo IIIA from a IIIB?
opciones: The size of the skin wound
The presence of arterial injury
That the IIIB requires a flap to cover the exposed bone
The high-energy mechanism
autoevaluacion.explicacion: Both are high energy and > 10 cm. The IIIA keeps adequate bone cover by soft tissue; the IIIB has periosteal stripping and bone exposure that demands a flap (fix and flap). Arterial injury defines the IIIC.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: In an open fracture, what weighs most on the risk of infection?
opciones: The time elapsed until theatre
The time elapsed until antibiotics
The type of implant chosen
The patient's position on the table
autoevaluacion.explicacion: The evidence supports early antibiotics; the classic 6-hour limit to debridement is not well supported.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: What are the components of the lethal triad?
opciones: Hypotension, tachycardia and oliguria
Coagulopathy, hypothermia and acidosis
SIRS, ARDS and multi-organ failure
Anaemia, hypoxaemia and hypercapnia
autoevaluacion.explicacion: Coagulopathy (INR > 1.5, platelets < 100,000, fibrinogen < 150), hypothermia (< 33 °C, which worsens it) and acidosis (pH < 7.25, which inhibits the clotting enzymes). They feed one another.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: Tibial fracture with increasing pain despite escalating opioids and severe pain on passive stretch of the toes. What do you do?
opciones: Elevate the limb, ice and reassess in 6 hours
Request an urgent MRI to confirm
Immediate decompressive fasciotomy
Increase the analgesia and watch the distal pulses
autoevaluacion.explicacion: Pain out of proportion and pain on passive stretch are the early, reliable signs. In the assessable patient the clinical picture is enough: there is no intermediate course and no investigation that should delay decompression. Elevating the limb actually lowers the perfusion pressure.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: An intubated, sedated patient with a leg fracture. The diastolic pressure is 70 mmHg and the measured compartment pressure 45 mmHg. What does that mean?
opciones: Normal: the compartment pressure is below 50 mmHg
ΔP = 25 mmHg — an indication for fasciotomy
Repeat the measurement in 4 hours
It cannot be judged without the systolic pressure
autoevaluacion.explicacion: ΔP = diastolic pressure − compartment pressure = 70 − 45 = 25 mmHg. Below 30 mmHg is an indication for fasciotomy. In the patient who cannot be assessed, the measurement replaces the clinical picture.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: A 5 mm entry wound from a gunshot to the leg, with a tibial fracture. Which Gustilo type?
opciones: Type I, because the wound is under 1 cm
Type II, because it is a diaphyseal fracture
Type III, because a bullet reclassifies by definition
It depends on the calibre of the bullet
autoevaluacion.explicacion: The skin hole does not reflect the damage: the kinetic energy is dissipated along the track, producing cavitation, deep devitalisation and dragged clothing and contaminants. The whole track has to be explored, not just the holes.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: Which of these is NOT part of a correct fasciotomy?
opciones: Decompressing all four compartments of the leg through a two-incision approach
Assessing muscle viability with the 4 Cs
Closing the skin primarily to reduce the risk of infection
Watching for rhabdomyolysis and renal function after reperfusion
autoevaluacion.explicacion: It is not closed primarily: closure is delayed and progressive, or by graft, once the swelling settles. Closing it straight away undoes the decompression. And a short fasciotomy is an incomplete fasciotomy.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: An 82-year-old patient with a low-energy fracture. What does that mean for the plan beyond the fixation?
opciones: Nothing different: the fracture pattern dictates the treatment
It is a sentinel event: it demands adapted anchorage and secondary prevention
It contraindicates surgery on the grounds of chronological age
It always mandates an arthroplasty
autoevaluacion.explicacion: A fragility fracture announces the next one. What matters is physiological age, not chronological, and osteoporotic bone demands specific anchoring strategies.
